t:
This title does not appy to—

    (1) 
any standards activity engaged in by any Federal agency or State agency for the use (including, but not limited to, use with respect to research and development, production, or consumption) of that agency or the use of another such agency; or
 
    (2) 
any standards activity engaged in by any private person solely for use in the production or consumption of products by that person.

fable.w: This section only carves out exemptions from the title's coverage for certain standards activities by federal or state agencies and by private persons for their own use. The mention of State agencies and private persons could tempt a Yes reading, but they appear only as subjects of the exemption, not as parties consulted or heard in any federal decision. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: This title does not appy to—

opus.w: This section is an exemption that lists standards activities to which the title does not apply. Even though it mentions State agencies and private persons, it does not have the federal government consult or coordinate with them before making a decision. Naming outside actors in a list of exemptions is not participation.
opus.s: This title does not appy to—
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this section involves outside parties, since it names "State agency" and "private person." That fails the definition: the section only exempts certain standards activities from the title. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the scope of the title by excluding certain activities, specifically those of federal/state agencies for internal use and private persons for sole internal use. It does not establish any mechanism for outside parties to consult with, comment on, or participate in federal decision-making processes. The exclusion of private persons from the title's application does not constitute a requirement for their participation in federal decisions.
qwen_chat.s: This title does not appy to— (1) any standards activity engaged in by any Federal agency or State agency for the use (including, but not limited to, use with respect to research and development, production, or consumption) of that agency or the use of another such agency; or (2) any standards activity engaged in by any private person solely for use in the production or consumption of products by that person.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that excluding "private persons" from the scope of the title implies that private persons are otherwise involved in standards activities, and thus participation is relevant. However, the section itself is a scope limitation clause that defines what is *not* covered. It does not establish a process for private persons to participate in federal decision-making; rather, it exempts certain private activities from federal regulation. There is no requirement for consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties in this specific text.
